commit message:
Updated exercise 4

This commit updates exercise 4. Parts where solutions are found from R demos are removed, and
parts about computing MCSEs are added. Rubric is also updated. No longer needed functions
and markmyassignment tests are removed.

This commit also adds the mcse_quantile function to the aaltobda package.
This function is used in the exercise to compute MCSE of quantiles for independent draws.
The function is a simplified version of a similar function from the loo package,
but now instead of effective samples size, the actual sample size is used.

between the original and new clustering code and verifies that they're the

implemented in the snn_helper and snn_vectorized files but will be deleted in the

commit message:
add additional tests for CDEs

cde_behavior_test is the start of a test suite for ML behavioral
testing. Right now, the only test it contains checks that the training
loss goes down over time for each CDE.

cde_regression_test compares the output of the CDE to a saved, "correct"
result. Since the results of the CDEs are pretty variable, this test
calculates the mean for each feature from the CDE output, and checks
that they are equal between arrays within a 15% relative tolerance (see numpy
allclose for details on what that means).

commit message:
Replacing loose file permission with stricter permission

# What is wrong?

In file: [hosts.py](https://github.com/vatlab/sos/blob/master/src/sos/hosts.py#L77) in class `DaemonizedProcess` method `run()` sets umask value to `0` that grants full permission to all users except the owner and the member of the groups instead of setting the value to default value of the system. When permissions settings for a resource are configured to provide access to a broader spectrum of individuals or entities than is truly essential, it opens the possibility of sensitive data being exposed or the resource being altered by unintended or unauthorized parties. This underscores the significance of implementing precise and tailored permissions to uphold data security and resource integrity. More information is available in: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/732.html

# Proposed Fix

Instead of using `os.umask(0)` which can be dangerous, use the system's default umask value

```python
- os.umask(0)
+ os.umask(os.umask(0))
```

- Bug fix pull request

- /src/sos/hosts.py

Alpha-Omega is a project partnering with open source software project maintainers to systematically find new, as-yet-undiscovered vulnerabilities in open source code - and get them fixed - to improve global software supply chain security.

The bug is found by running the iCR tool by [OpenRefactory, Inc.](https://openrefactory.com/) and then manually triaging the results.
